question.prompt: The orthocenter of a triangle is the concurrent intersection of the three (possibly extended) altitudes. What is the sum of the coordinates of the orthocenter of the triangle whose vertices are \(A(2, 31),\) \(B(8, 27),\) and \(C(18, 27)?\)

solutions.title: Intersect two altitude lines
solutions.explanation:
Because \(B\) and \(C\) have the same vertical coordinate, \(BC\) is horizontal. Its perpendicular altitude through \(A(2,31)\) is therefore the vertical line
\[
x=2.
\]
We only need one more altitude to locate the orthocenter.

The slope of \(AB\) is
\[
\frac{27-31}{8-2}=-\frac46=-\frac23.
\]
The altitude through \(C\) is perpendicular to \(AB\), so its slope is the negative reciprocal, \(\frac32\). Since it passes through \(C(18,27)\), its equation is
\[
y-27=\frac32(x-18).
\]
Expanding the right side gives \(y-27=\frac32x-27\), so
\[
y=\frac32x.
\]
At its intersection with \(x=2\), we have \(y=\frac32\cdot2=3\). Thus the orthocenter is \((2,3)\), and the requested sum is
\[
2+3=\boxed{5},
\]
choice A.
